newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM, METSA-SERLA DEALS SLIGHT PULP CAPACITY BOOST.
newsitem.headline: UPM, METSA-SERLA DEALS SLIGHT PULP CAPACITY BOOST.

text.p: Finnish forestry groups UPM-Kymmene Oy and Metsa-Serla Oy said on Tuesday their total annual pulp output would rise only slightly from a series of deals, but Metsa-Botnia's pulp capacity would surge.

Overall, the two firms' combined pulp output capacity would rise 30,000 tonnes to 4.23 million tonnes. The entire rise would stem from the modernisation of Joutseno Pulp, due to be sold by UPM-Kymmene to pulp producer Metsa-Botnia, they said.
Together, Metsa-Serla and its parent, the forest owners' cooperative Metsaliitto, hold 53 percent of Metsa-Botnia with UPM-Kymmene owning the remaining 47 percent.
Metsa-Botnia's annual pulp output capacity will increase by 780,000 tonnes to 2.36 million tonnes. Of this the Joutseno acquisition will account for 320,000 tonnes.
The transfer by Metsa-Serla of its Aanekoski pulp mill to Metsa-Botnia will account for 460,000 tonnes.
When the Joutseno upgrade investment comes on stream Metsa-Botnia's annual chemical pulp output capacity will rise to 2.39 million tonnes.
Based on its stake in Metsa-Botnia, UPM-Kymmene said its self-supply of chemical pulp would rise by about 50,000 tonnes but it gave no further details.
